title: remotes and the daily loop
goal: B2 fetch, pull and push — and knowing which one you meant
startWith: Use a remote you can push to: a scratch repo on GitHub, or a bare repo on disk (git init --bare ../lab-remote.git).

newIdeas.plain: A named URL. origin is a convention, not a keyword.
origin/main is your last-known copy of the remote's branch. Only fetch updates it.
fetch plus merge (or rebase). Two operations wearing one name.

tasks.do: Add a remote and push a branch with upstream tracking

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git remote add origin <url>
git remote -v
git push -u origin main

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Ctrl+Shift+K is Push. The dialog shows exactly what will go and lets you pick the remote branch.

tasks.do: Fetch, then look before you merge
tasks.why: fetch is always safe — it changes no file you are working on. pull is fetch plus a merge you did not read first.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git fetch origin
git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main    # what would come in
git diff HEAD origin/main --stat
git merge origin/main

tasks.do: Configure pull to rebase, and understand what you just chose
tasks.why: Merge-pull litters shared history with “Merge branch main of …” commits nobody wrote on purpose.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git config --global pull.rebase true
git config --global rebase.autoStash true
git config --get pull.rebase

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Ctrl+T (Update Project) asks merge or rebase the first time and remembers. Change it in Settings → Version Control → Git → Update method.

tasks.do: Amend a pushed commit and push it again safely
tasks.why: --force-with-lease refuses when someone else pushed in the meantime; --force does not care.

check.run: # never force-push a shared branch without telling people first
check.expect: you can say what force-with-lease protects

tasks.do: Prune remote branches that no longer exist

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git fetch --prune
git remote prune origin --dry-run

proof.note: Your branch knows its upstream and you can read the ahead/behind counts.

doneWhen: You never type git pull without knowing whether it will merge or rebase.

lessons.title: Update Project (Ctrl+T)
lessons.teach: Ctrl+T is fetch + integrate. The first run asks merge or rebase and then remembers, so make that choice deliberately — it is the pull.rebase setting you just configured.

lessons.title: Push (Ctrl+Shift+K)
lessons.teach: Ctrl+Shift+K shows exactly which commits will go and to which remote branch — the confirmation the terminal makes you build yourself with git log HEAD..origin/main. Force push is in the dropdown next to the button, and IntelliJ uses --force-with-lease.
